body: Looks like these bools are swapped. Probably why it doesn't work.
I notice that the reflection colour in the Compatibility screenshots is off from the background colour, is it correct to convert this to linear encoding?

Without this sRGB -> linear conversion, it's even brighter: The issue seems to be the sky color; it appears too dark compared to Forward+/Mobile. The reflection color appears identical to Forward+/Mobile in comparison (`#00a27a`).

Hmm, background colour is fine for me, but the rendering is darker for Compatibility: Background mode | Compatibility | Forward+ --|-- | -- Custom color | | Procedural sky | | Compared to 4.6 Beta 2, this is not a new issue: Background mode | Compatibility | Forward+ --|-- | -- Custom color | | Procedural sky | | Which has lead me to discover that there are very different results between using the editor directional light preview vs. adding a directional light in Compatibility: Light | Compatibility | Forward+ --|-- | -- Scene light | | Editor preview light | | And again, this is not new. These screenshots are with **4.6 Beta 2**: Light | Compatibility | Forward+ --|-- | -- Scene light | | Editor preview light | | 😵‍💫 So all that to say, this PR seems to do some things correctly, but it doesn't fix all of the existing issues T_T Here's my test project: [black-reflections.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24300490/black-reflections.zip)

@Allenwp the editor preview light problem you are referring to is the difference between shadows enabled / disabled and is expected because the light is mixed in srgb space for performance reasons when shadows are enabled. I believe the reason why with shadows disabled it looks different than Forward+ is due to metallic so I don't know if it's related to this pr.

@Calinou `bg_energy_multiplier` should be multiplied into `color` after converting to linear.

Also I figured out that the issue with the background colour appearing darker is because you probably have tonemapping enabled which doesn't affect the background colour in Compatibility, I made a pr a while ago to fix it which hasn't been approved: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/111550 .
I'm thinking that `specular_light *= scene_data_block.data.ambient_light_color_energy.a;` should probably happen for both background colour and sky modes?

> @Calinou `bg_energy_multiplier` should be multiplied into `color` after converting to linear.

Where should this be done?
